extracted.intended_audience: scientists (including early-career researchers), journal editors, scientific societies, publishers, and academic institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and implementing structured training programs to teach scientists how to perform high-quality, fair, and civil peer review (includes curricula, calibration, mentoring, and institutional/publisher responsibilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit bias training and testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach about and test for implicit bias rather than assuming this training occurs elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data indicate bias in scientific peer review results in biased publication outcomes but awareness of bias can mitigate it; include instruction and testing on implicit bias (reference to Stanford Plato entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Didactic instruction on the science of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce scientists to the peer review literature, history, common problems in the process, and data-driven solutions to pitfalls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over 25,000 articles on 'peer review' exist; courses should use this literature to teach the evidence base and empirical findings about peer review practices and failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction on use of community-wide resources on peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach individuals to consult and use established community guidelines (e.g., COPE) and journal-specific reviewer guidance before accepting invitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover COPE ethical guidelines and journal-specific instructions (e.g., ASM reviewer guidelines); trainees should learn to check journal scope, scoring rubrics/templates, and expectations about significance/impact prior to agreeing to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction on how to evaluate a manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach how to evaluate manuscripts for author bias, statistical rigor, adequacy of controls, reproducibility of methods, transparency of data, adequacy of reference lists, how well data support conclusions, and adequacy of discussion of study limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use checklists as safeguards against bias and to standardize evaluations; include focused training in evaluation of study execution and use of resources (scoring rubrics/checklists) to improve detection of statistical and methodological issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation using calibration exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a set of training/test manuscripts to evaluate whether scientists can detect common errors and to calculate inter-rater reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use calibration exercises to determine which scientific errors reviewers commonly fail to detect; adapt course content or checklists based on inter-rater reliability scores; calibrating reviewers enables quantitative assessment of ability to identify omissions (e.g., missing controls, improper statistical tests, missing sequence deposition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction on how to write a peer review (structure & style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach the content and style of peer reviews: an introductory paragraph summarizing findings and significance; major comments outlining revision requests addressing deficiencies in scientific rigor; minor comments to improve readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use published public peer reviews or instructor-generated examples to demonstrate what belongs in major vs minor comments and to evaluate sufficiency of introductory summaries; emphasize appropriate professional tone and evaluate examples in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction on the ethics of scientific publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover the peer reviewer's role in safeguarding against scientific misconduct, common biases in manuscripts, and ethical responsibilities of peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach identification and reporting of misconduct (e.g., plagiarism, image manipulation) and ethical boundaries of reviewer behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction on communication with editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach appropriate use of the confidential note to editors, other bounds surrounding communications with editors, when to decline a review, and how to report alleged scientific misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address common misuse or under-use of confidential notes; provide clear examples of appropriate vs inappropriate content for editor communications and protocols for reporting problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction of civility and professional communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce civility, inter-generational views of civility, and norms of professional communications in science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide theory, structured examples, and discussion of appropriate/inappropriate phrasing, tone, and commentary; emphasize avoiding personal attacks and the disproportionate harm uncivil reviews do to early-career and historically excluded researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term, structured mentoring and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sustained mentoring whereby trainees evaluate multiple manuscripts and receive feedback on review quality and process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apprenticeship models are common but variable; programs (e.g., mBio Junior Editorial Board) can include mentored reviews evaluated by editors. Evidence suggests short interventions yield minimal long-term improvements, so longer structured mentoring is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective scoring rubrics and inter-rater reliability for review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and use objective scoring rubrics/checklists for editors to rate peer review quality and to improve inter-rater agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors often evaluate subjectively with only modest agreement; structured rubrics/checklists can increase transparency and standardization of review quality assessments and should be taught/implemented as part of training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in statistical and epidemiological analysis / use of statistical expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide focused training in statistical and epidemiological analysis or provide access to statistical expertise to improve reviewers' ability to detect methodological/statistical flaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background in statistical or epidemiological analysis predicts higher editorial ratings of review quality; journals could consider hiring dedicated statistical editors who vet manuscripts; training should target evaluation of study execution and statistical rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach journal-specific scope and reviewer expectations before accepting invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Train reviewers to consult and align with each journal's specific standards (scope, acceptable requests, scoring templates) before accepting review invitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance differs between journals; understanding journal-specific peer review guidelines helps avoid overreaching requests (e.g., asking for experiments outside journal scope) and misuse of confidential notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance implementation considerations and stakeholder coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the potential trade-offs of requiring training (e.g., reducing reviewer pool) and risks of fragmented, inconsistent training across societies and publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation requires buy-in (funding, rewards, external pressure) and coordination among stakeholders (publishers, societies, institutions); weigh costs (time, willingness) and design scalable programs to avoid fragmentation.
